query:
Someone in the family expressed a preference for using ingredients sourced directly from Nigeria rather than imported substitutes. Who made this point, and what in how they expressed it tells you it was their observation rather than the family member who agreed?

Options:
A. Uncle Dele
B. Adaeze
C. Emeka
D. Seun
context:
[1] (about=Uncle Dele, episodic, t0 @2025-01-06T19:50:00) EMEKA is correct. Imported ingredients are not a substitute for the real thing. I will say no more on that. Best regards, Dele
[2] (about=Emeka, episodic, t0 @2025-01-06T19:47:00) Good. The fish was from Nigeria last trip. Worth it.
[3] (about=Adaeze, core, t14 @2025-02-24T19:02:00) Adaeze has been experimenting with her recipes since Seun told them about her results, including making egusi with coconut oil and mushrooms last week
[4] (about=Adaeze, said_by=Seun, profile, t14 @2025-02-24T19:02:00) Seun tells Adaeze that her veganism was oyinbo food last year, and now she approves of Adaeze's vegan recipes
[5] (about=Nkem, episodic, t4 @2025-01-20T20:20:00) I think this is wonderful, Seun. I may be wrong but the research on plant-forward diets and inflammation is quite compelling. Did your GP mention the specific markers?
[6] (about=Seun, said_by=Tolu, core, t4 @2025-01-20T20:02:00) Seun will separate the B12 in yeast extract from her jollof rice
[7] (about=Seun, core, t6 @2025-01-27T17:02:00) Seun will separate the B12 in yeast extract from her jollof rice
[8] (about=Tolu, episodic, t4 @2025-01-20T20:38:00) Mum, the B12 is in yeast extract. Clinically speaking Seun will be fine. The bigger challenge is family dinners where the protein is not separated.

query:
Two family members made essentially the same observation about Emeka needing rest after a demanding day — one grounding it in shared experience, the other in clinical reasoning. Who made the shared-experience framing, and what specifically distinguishes their message from the other person's?

Options:
A. Tolu
B. Auntie Grace
C. Adaeze
D. Uncle Dele
context:
[1] (about=Tolu, episodic, t6 @2025-01-27T17:36:00) Clinically speaking, rest after exertion is appropriate. Just to note, Dad - if this is a pattern we should talk.
[2] (about=Seun, episodic, t6 @2025-01-27T17:29:00) honestly Dad you should rest though I mean you were on your feet most of yesterday
[3] (about=Adaeze, said_by=Emeka, core, t14 @2025-02-24T19:02:00) Emeka notes that Dad was tired from yesterday and missed church
[4] (about=Adaeze, core, t14 @2025-02-24T19:02:00) Adaeze asks Emeka to sort oxtail
[5] (about=Auntie Grace, core, t6 @2025-01-27T17:02:00) Auntie Grace notes that many patients push through when they should be resting
[6] (about=Auntie Grace, said_by=Seun, profile, t14 @2025-02-24T19:02:00) Seun reminds Auntie Grace that conversations about rest and listening to her body stayed with her and led to her taking a holiday alone since 2021
[7] (about=Emeka, core, t6 @2025-01-27T17:02:00) Emeka notes that Dad was tired from yesterday and missed church
[8] (about=Emeka, core, t2 @2025-01-13T18:32:00) Oxtail. I will sort it
[9] (about=Funke, episodic, t4 @2025-01-20T20:32:00) EMEKA 💀 said what he said 😂
[10] (about=Kayode, episodic, t6 @2025-01-27T17:14:00) Thought he was tired from yesterday?
[11] (about=Nkem, episodic, t6 @2025-01-27T17:23:00) I think it is quite natural after a full day like yesterday - I may be wrong but the drive back alone must have been tiring. Did the Sunday call happen this afternoon?
[12] (about=Uncle Dele, core, t6 @2025-01-27T17:02:00) Uncle Dele notes that Emeka has always been disciplined about his health
[13] (about=Uncle Dele, core, t6 @2025-01-27T17:02:00) Uncle Dele trusts Emeka and notes he is well, rest is important at their age
agent_answer: D. Uncle Dele — his message is distinguished by grounding rest in shared age/life experience (“rest is important at their age”) rather than Tolu’s clinical reasoning (“Clinically speaking…”).
